principles: One canonical REVIEW contract must eliminate drift across five reviewer templates.
Agent guidance projects System semantics but never replaces mechanical gate facts.
Scope is determined by applicability and gate impact, not severity alone.
Tests must demonstrate delivery and isolation before digest pins are accepted.
drivers: Five active reviewer lanes and two envelope paths need byte-consistent behavior.
Open-source English quality and compatibility with legacy prompt assembly are required.
The authoritative Dynamic Finding plan must remain unchanged.

options.name: Central resolver injection
cons: Requires focused assembly tests and pin refresh

options.name: Edit each reviewer template
pros: Behavior visible in each source template
cons: Legacy restoration hashes and templates all change

rationale: Resolve the selected base body first, then append one canonical contract only when the active role is one of the five modular REVIEW lanes. Keep Owner and implementer guidance at their own authority boundaries and add REVIEW-only declarative metadata.

preMortem.scenario: Contract leaks into Story Owner or implementer prompts
preMortem.trigger: Injection uses modular-role detection instead of reviewer-role detection
preMortem.consequence: Non-REVIEW Agents receive unauthorized reviewer behavior
preMortem.mitigation: Add adversarial isolation assertions for every non-REVIEW modular role in both modes.

preMortem.scenario: Prompt prose is mistaken for a new gate implementation
preMortem.trigger: Documentation or metadata claims the triage check was executed or blocking changed
preMortem.mitigation: State declarative-only semantics and run process-fact contract verification without touching Dynamic Finding runtime files.

preMortem.trigger: Contract is appended only on the modular source path
preMortem.consequence: Mixed rollout produces divergent reviewer behavior
preMortem.mitigation: Resolve base body first and append after mode selection; assert both modes contain the same contract.

preMortem.scenario: High/critical out-of-scope findings become silently dismissed
preMortem.trigger: Prompt equates routing or compatibility dismissal with resolution
preMortem.consequence: Serious defects lose ownership and audit history
preMortem.mitigation: Require evidence-backed route and owner, preserve original finding, and explicitly deny dismissal as applicability proof.

preMortem.scenario: Digest refresh blesses an unintended prompt change
preMortem.trigger: Pins are updated before semantic assertions and RED/GREEN tests
preMortem.consequence: Baseline verifier goes green despite behavior regression
preMortem.mitigation: Run focused RED/GREEN semantic tests first, inspect generated diffs, then repin and rerun baselines.
